neighbours.label: the word right after the 'be' of a fused relative 'what' ('what was a', 'what had been an', 'what were', French 'ce qu'est un'); the same clauses with 'that', 'which is' or no 'what' stay quiet
fire: Rain ruined what had been a pleasant afternoon at the fair.
The guide explained what was an unusual custom in the valley.
Critics praised what is a bold second novel by the author.
He sold what had been a thriving shop on the corner.
Soldiers burned what was once a prosperous village by the river.
Her essay covers what were, in her view, the main causes of the war.
Ce livre explique ce qu'est une constitution et pourquoi elle compte.
They turned what looked like a dull lecture into a party.
quiet: Rain ruined that pleasant afternoon at the fair on Sunday.
The guide explained that this was an unusual custom in the valley.
Critics praised this bold second novel by the author.
He sold his thriving shop on the corner to a cousin.
Soldiers burned a prosperous village by the river in spring.
Her essay covers, in her view, the main causes of the war.
Ce livre explique une constitution et pourquoi elle compte.
They turned that dull lecture into a party for everyone.
